newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Quick&Reilly to launch Internet page Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: Quick&Reilly to launch Internet page Nov 1.

text.p: Quick & Reilly discount brokers will launch an Internet Web site on November 1, but only expects to conduct around five percent of its business on the network, Quick & Reilly Group Inc Chairman Leslie Quick said.

"We have a Web site and we will be going up on Internet on the first of November. We have been working on that project for the last six months...It does work and we are ready to roll," Quick told the Swiss-American Chamber of Commerce.

"Our problem basically is pricing. We are sort of in the same position as Merrill Lynch was when we came into the discount brokerage business and started offering 70 percent off on trades against their prices."
Quick said trading via the Internet would probably make up only a small part of the company's total business.

"I would say probably five percent," he said, adding the potential customer base was limited to the relatively small, but growing ranks of computer-literate investors whose typical business differed from that of standard retail customers.

"What we see in the product mix is that basically the people who are trading on Internet or through Internet on a PC (personal computer) are a different breed of cat than we have experienced in the retail business in general," he said.
"We find they are doing 20 percent options, probably about 42 to 44 percent over the counter (stocks), they are doing 20 percent listed (shares) and the rest is mutual funds and bonds.
"It is a different mix. We do probably 55 percent listed business with our retail side," he said.
Internet-driven business can also pose problems for brokers who specialise in this area, however.

"They are different kind of people. My feeling is that they work on such very slim margins that, if we get a major dip in the marketplace, they are going to have a very difficult time staying in business," he added.
